name: 47C04-E_SN
title: 47L04/47C04/47L16/47C16: 4-Kbit and 16-Kbit I2C serial EERAM (SRAM with EEPROM backup)
summary: A byte-wide SRAM on an I2C bus up to 1 MHz, backed by an EEPROM of equal size: 512 x 8 in the 47X04 and 2,048 x 8 in the 47X16. SRAM reads and writes are unlimited; the data is copied to EEPROM on power loss from a capacitor on VCAP (Auto-Store), on a pulse at the HS pin, or by command, and is copied back at power-up. The 47L parts run from 2.7 V to 3.6 V and the 47C parts from 4.5 V to 5.5 V. 47C04-E/SN is the 4-Kbit 5 V part rated -40 °C to +125 °C in an 8-lead SOIC.
key_figures: 4.0 V to 4.4 V (47CXX), 2.4 V to 2.6 V (47LXX)
200 µA typ, 400 µA max at 5.5 V, 1 MHz

notes: Full order codes take the form 47C04T-E/SN. Examples: 47L04-E/P, 47L04-E/SN, 47L04-I/ST, 47L04T-E/SN, 47L04T-I/ST, 47C04-E/P, 47C04-E/SN, 47C04-I/ST, 47C04T-E/SN, 47C04T-I/ST, 47L16-E/P, 47L16-E/SN, 47L16-I/ST, 47L16T-E/SN, 47L16T-I/ST, 47C16-E/P, 47C16-E/SN, 47C16-I/ST, 47C16T-E/SN, 47C16T-I/ST; automotive 47C16-E/SN16KVAO and 47C16T-E/SN16KVAO.
47C04-E/SN is the 4-Kbit, 5 V part, extended temperature (-40°C to +125°C), in the 8-lead SOIC, in standard packaging (tube or tray).
Temperature ranges: I = -40°C to +85°C, E = -40°C to +125°C. Packages: P = 8-lead PDIP, SN = 8-lead SOIC, ST = 8-lead TSSOP. The automotive parts come in SN and ST only, E range.
47X04 means 47L04 and 47C04; 47X16 means 47L16 and 47C16; 47LXX the 3 V parts and 47CXX the 5 V parts.

pins.name: VCAP
pins.function: Capacitor input, tied to the internal supply bus. With Auto-Store, CVCAP goes from this pin to VSS and charges from VCC; it powers the store when VCC is lost. Without a capacitor, connect VCAP to VCC and clear ASE.

pins.name: A1
pins.function: Chip select input, matched against the A1 bit of the client address. Pulled down internally to VSS when left open.

pins.name: A2
pins.function: Chip select input, matched against the A2 bit of the client address. Pulled down internally to VSS when left open.

pins.name: SDA
pins.function: Serial data, bidirectional, for addresses and data. Open drain: it needs a pull-up to VCC, typically 10 kΩ at 100 kHz and 2 kΩ at 400 kHz or 1 MHz. Schmitt trigger input.

pins.name: SCL
pins.function: Serial clock input that times every transfer. Schmitt trigger input.

pins.name: HS
pins.function: Hardware Store / event detect input. A high pulse of at least THSPW starts a Hardware Store (when AM = 1) and sets the EVENT bit. Ignored during store and recall and while VCAP is below VTRIP. Pulled down internally to VSS when left open.

circuits.title: Typical application, Auto-Store mode (ASE = 1)
circuits.description: A microcontroller drives the I2C bus, SCL and SDA, each pulled up to VCC by its own resistor, and drives HS from a third line to trigger hardware stores. VCC has a bypass capacitor to ground. CVCAP from VCAP to ground holds the charge that lets the part copy its SRAM into EEPROM when VCC goes away. A1 and A2 are not connected, so the internal pull-downs give chip select 00.

parts.note: SDA pull-up; typically 10 kΩ at 100 kHz, 2 kΩ at 400 kHz and 1 MHz

notes: ASE must be 1 in the STATUS register for the store on power loss.

circuits.title: Typical application, Manual Store mode (ASE = 0)
circuits.description: The same bus hookup as Auto-Store mode, with no capacitor on VCAP: VCAP joins VCC, which has a bypass capacitor to ground. Data reaches EEPROM only through HS or a software store command, and Auto-Store has to be off (ASE = 0). A1 and A2 are open, pulled down inside the part.

parts.note: SDA pull-up; typically 10 kΩ at 100 kHz, 2 kΩ at 400 kHz and 1 MHz

notes: Power must not fail during a store in this mode, or EEPROM data can be corrupted.

operation.text: An SRAM that is read and written over I2C with no limit on cycles, shadowed by an EEPROM of the same size. Copying SRAM to EEPROM is a store; copying back is a recall. Only the SRAM is reachable from the bus.

The part is an I2C client; the host makes Start and Stop and the clock. A transfer starts only on an idle bus (both lines high). SDA may change only while SCL is low; SDA falling with SCL high is Start, rising with SCL high is Stop. Every command begins with Start and ends with Stop. The receiver pulls SDA low in the ninth clock to acknowledge each byte; the host ends a read by leaving that bit high on the last byte. Clock rates of 100 kHz, 400 kHz and 1 MHz; reads and writes have no cycle delay.

Op code 1010 reaches the SRAM array, 0011 the control registers. The A2 and A1 bits of the control byte are compared with the A2 and A1 pin levels, so four parts can share one bus. While VCAP is below VTRIP the part answers nothing.

After a write control byte, two address bytes follow, most significant first, and load the address pointer (the top five bits of the high byte are don't care, and on the 47X04 the next two as well). Each data byte is latched into SRAM on the rising SCL edge of its acknowledge, and the pointer steps by one. Writes may run on without limit; at the end of the array the pointer wraps to 0x000. A write that is cut short keeps every byte already acknowledged.

A data byte aimed at a protected address gets no acknowledge; the operation stops, the pointer does not move, and SDA is ignored until the next Start. The same happens when a sequential write runs into a protected block.

A read control byte carries no address; reading starts at the pointer. Current address read: one byte, the host does not acknowledge and sends Stop. Random read: send a write control byte and two address bytes, then a repeated Start and a read control byte. Sequential read: the host acknowledges each byte to get the next; the pointer wraps to 0x000 at the end, so the whole array can be read in one go.

A control register write is the 0011 write control byte, one register address byte and data. An address other than 00h or 55h is not acknowledged and ends the operation. STATUS accepts any value, and when several data bytes are sent the last one is kept. COMMAND takes exactly one byte, 33h or DDh; any other value or extra bytes are refused and the operation is dropped. A control register read always returns STATUS, repeated for as long as the host acknowledges. After the Stop, wait TWC for a STATUS write, TSTORE for a software store or TRECALL for a software recall.

AM is set by any SRAM write and cleared when a store or recall completes; it is read-only and volatile, and Auto-Store and Hardware Store run only while it is 1. BP2-BP0 set the write-protected top part of the array, from 1/64 to all of it. ASE enables Auto-Store. EVENT is set by a pulse on HS and can also be written. BP, ASE and EVENT are nonvolatile: after a STATUS write the part spends TWC writing them and does not respond. A store triggered during that write cycle waits for it to finish and then uses the new ASE value.

Needs CVCAP on VCAP and ASE = 1. CVCAP charges from VCC. When VCAP falls below VTRIP the part runs from the capacitor and stores SRAM to EEPROM, only if AM = 1. It cannot be reached for TSTORE afterwards even if power returns. A store once started always finishes.

A rising edge on HS, held high for THSPW or more, starts a store when AM = 1, followed by a STATUS write that sets EVENT; the part is busy for TSTORE + TWC. With AM = 0 only the EVENT write runs, busy for TWC. HS is edge triggered: holding it high does not block access, and a second store needs HS taken low and high again. HS is ignored during store and recall and while VCAP is below VTRIP; EVENT is then not set.
Writing 33h to COMMAND stores SRAM to EEPROM whatever the state of AM and ASE; the part is busy for TSTORE. Writing DDh recalls EEPROM into SRAM; busy for TRECALL. Both clear AM at the end.

At power-up, once VCAP first climbs past VTRIP following a power-on reset, EEPROM is copied into SRAM regardless of ASE, and the part is busy for TRECALL. AM is cleared when it ends. If power is lost during the recall it is abandoned and no Auto-Store follows. SRAM contents hold as long as VCC stays above VPOR.
An Auto-Store or Hardware Store that triggers during an SRAM or control register access ends that access so the store can run.
Connect VCAP to VCC and write ASE to 0; otherwise EEPROM data can be corrupted on power loss. In this mode power must stay up through any store.

The part does not acknowledge during a store, a recall or a STATUS write cycle. To find the end, send Start and a write control byte (SRAM or control register) and repeat until it is acknowledged, then go on with the next command.
A1, A2 and HS each have a two-strength pull-down to VSS: strong (50 kΩ min) below VIL, weak (750 kΩ min) above VIH.
VCC must rise and fall no faster than 70 µs/V.
